Posted May 1, 2001
(MarijuanaNews note: Canada has a much smaller problem with politicized police than does DEAland – which is why I call it DEAland.

Nonetheless, the Mounties have their own narks, which I call the Royal Canadian Marijuana Police. These, in turn, have their special prohibitionist propagandist specialists, called " Drug Awareness " officers. Their DEAland counterparts are called " Demand Reduction Coordinators. "

For other examples see
Police Interference in the Canadian Electoral Process. The Royal Canadian Marijuana Police Disinformation Campaign for Marijuana Prohibition. Analysis by Richard Cowan.
and
 " It's Time To Declare Peace, " Says Great Canadian Op-ed. But Can Canada Escape the DEAland Marijuana Prohibition Trap, As the Mounties Lie To Keep the War Going? -- 2 items
and
As Canadian Senate Gets Ready To Study Prohibition, Canadian Police Push Prohibitionist Propaganda At Taxpayer Expense. 4 Items


(MarijuanaNews note: Chilliwack is a town in British Columbia.

Robert Sharpe, who works for the The Lindesmith Center-Drug Policy Foundation in Washington has been remarkably successful in getting his very well-written letters published. The Chilliwack Times recently carried one in which he pointed out, " While Canadian schools are just beginning to implement DARE, schools in the U.S. are dropping the program. Every methodologically sound evaluation of DARE has found the program to be either ineffective or counterproductive. "

Of course, that is sacrilege to the DARE supporters in the police. Hence the following…)

DARE ISN'T THE BE ALL AND END ALL
By Sgt Bob Hall RCMP Drug Awareness

Editor:
Let me clarify, DARE is very strong in the U.S. and President Bush just declared April 11, National DARE day. This was to honour those communities, schools and police officers taking part in preventing kids from using drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: True enough. DARE is indeed " very strong in the U.S. " However, that was not the question. The question is whether it is effective, not whether it is " strong " or beloved of politicians. It is certainly both.)

Critics of the DARE program generally fall into three categories; drug legalization advocates, those who have their own drug prevention program and drug users.

(MarijuanaNews note: That ad hominem has been the DARE response to its critics for years, even after they knew that it was not working. Here are three other categories of critics, the US Surgeon General, the US National Academy of Sciences and the President of DARE, Glenn Levant, who said, " I'm not saying it was effective, but it was state of the art when we launched it. "
See
Even The Prohibitionists Are Attacking DARE. What Is the Definition of Fraud? Analysis By Richard Cowan

It is not surprising to me that your story last week made it to the Lindesmith Center in Washington DC because it advocates the legalization of marijuana. Does it make you wonder why an organization from the U.S. would be so concerned about us in Chilliwack?
(MarijuanaNews note: It is more than a little disingenuous to question why someone from " an organization from the U.S. " would raise questions about the effectiveness of a US based organization. Also the RCMP works closely with another " organization from the U.S " – the DEA. Also inasmuch as Canadians care about what happens in Tibet, it is not too strange that the few Americans who know where Canada is would care about its people and policies.)

I agree with Mr. Sharpe on a couple of points. Scare tactics don't work for all kids so that is why we don't use them in DARE. I would also agree with Mr. Sharpe on his point that the kids are being lied to about marijuana and you only need to read the letter to the editor written by Denise Ford to see that marijuana is a dangerous and addictive substance. See below.

Doctors of Addiction Medicine in British Columbia also confirm this. Research shows when the perceived risks of drug use is low, drug use rises and vice versa. When you talk to our young people you will quickly find out their perception of risk is low and it is because to the mixed messages they are hearing. I find it appalling to hear these messages repeated by some 10- and 11-year-olds in this community.
See
An Excellent Critique of DARE and " Drug Education " Misses One Key Point:
Lying About Marijuana Is Both Their Purpose and Their Undoing
and
How the War On Marijuana To Save The Children
Has Become A War On the Children To Save Marijuana Prohibition

The short-term positive outcomes of DARE are well supported in research. In fact, a research based guide to prevention identifies eight NIDA ( National Institute on Drug Abuse ) criteria for a successful program and DARE meets them all. DARE was never developed to be a stand alone program. As any parent would know, messages to our young people have to be consistent and reinforced to be effective. DARE is a primary prevention program which should form part of a much larger prevention strategy which promotes healthy, non-destructive behaviors. Let's move on and prevent kids from using drugs.



(MarijuanaNews note: An identical letter was published in the Chilliwack Progress.)

POT USE DANGEROUS

Editor:

I am very upset over the attitude most people have towards using pot. In the Friday, April 13th issue the Times, when teens were asked if they would report other teens using drugs, most responded with " If it's just pot then probably not. "

Where does this attitude come from? Pot is not what it was in the 60s, 70s or 80s.
See
Marijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety --
" Is Marijuana Stronger Than It Was Back In the '60s, When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless? " Analysis By Richard Cowan
and
RCMP Annual Report On the " Drug Situation in Canada " Contradicts Staples Of the Prohibitionist Party Line. Exclusive To MarijuanaNews.

It's usually laced with other drugs or the plants are sprayed with stronger illegal drugs.
(MarijuanaNews note: That is nonsense, but it is also an argument for legalization. Contamination is a characteristic of contraband markets, not an argument for prohibition.)

I'd like to let these teens come to my home and witness the physical and mental anguish a 17-year-old is going through after four weeks of not taking " just pot. "

I'd like these teens to tell him, " Hey man, pot can't hurt you " when every muscle and bone in his body is raging in pain, when he can't sleep because his head pounds incessantly and in the morning his whole body shakes for hours.
(MarijuanaNews note: Obviously, it is not marijuana withdrawal. Even barbiturate withdrawal does not last for four weeks. The Drug Czar’s own Institute of Medicine Report said, " A distinctive marijuana withdrawal syndrome has been identified, but it is mild and short-lived. "
See
Executive Summary Of The IOM Report, Marijuana And Medicine: Assessing The Science Base
and
Is Marijuana Addictive?
Analysis By Richard Cowan

When I first read this, I just assumed that the boy did not exist. I have become very cynical about the prohibitionists. However, if there really is such a child, he should be given immediate medical help, which is free in Canada, and this woman should be arrested for child endangerment.)

Tell him when the very sight of food makes his stomach churn and when he knows the only relief is for him to go smoke a joint but he's made a promise to himself to quit the " just pot " so he can have a life. Tell him when he fights a mental battle every moment with his addiction, when he blacks out or has memory losses.

I'd like those teens to go to Skid Row in Vancouver and ask each of the heroin addicts, whose mere skeletal bodies crowd the alleys, how they got that way. Every time, the answer will be " Oh, I started just with pot. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me, but if marijuana has such a dire withdrawal syndrome, the people on skid row would not have " started just with pot. " They would be there directly because of marijuana.)
See
 " Those who insist on keeping the plant illegal bear a serious degree of moral responsibility for young marijuana users who do go on to use cocaine, heroin, PCP or other genuinely dangerous or addictive drugs. " Alan Bock, of the Orange County Register On the Real Gateway
and
Marijuana Legalization, The Missing Pillar in Solving the Substance Abuse Problem in Vancouver and All of Canada. Analysis By Richard Cowan

It's time each of us opens our eyes and quit hiding behind the " just pot " is okay slogan. Legalize it? . . .You've got to be kidding.
See
Legalize Marijuana and Reduce Use?
New Survey Puts Estimate of Dutch Marijuana Use Even More Below DEAland
and
Legalize Marijuana and Improve High-School Academic Performance? Holland Ranks First – The US Very Low

Not unless you want this young generation of " pot heads " to run our country. Not me. I'm helping one teen at a time.
(MarijuanaNews note: How is she doing that? By depriving a seriously ill child needed medical care because she has decided that he is going through " marijuana withdrawal "? Of course, there are so many quacks in " addiction treatment " that he may be getting " medical care " and suffering another consequence of marijuana prohibition.)
Denise Ford,
Chilliwack
